corridor: wharf frontage: 200 native px inside sheet 11's bay-side neatline
why_not_one_block_off: Not a street. Sheet 11 draws the whole wharf yard at 50 ft/in right up to its bay-side neatline (tracks, the slip, the wharf-front blocks), so it owns everything it maps; the seam sits 200 native px (~70 ft) inside its neatline, and the min-ink path within the band settles where the wharf plate's pier sheds end and the block plate's yard begins, as the master's yard cut (D-020) did. The wharf plate supplies only the piers and bay beyond.
solve_note: seam position, not a feature tie: a_native/b_native are 'this many px inside the block plate's neatline' and the wharf plate's matching x, so the pair is where to CUT, not two readings of one feature. Excluded from least-squares solves (tools/localsolve.py, tools/bandresid.py); still read by tools/streetcut.py.
